findings.affected_surface: user-visible daemon output (IP address for IPv6 clients)
findings.old_behavior: When getaddrinfo() returns an AF_INET6 (IPv6) address, lookup_hostname() casts ai->ai_addr to struct sockaddr_in* and reads sin_addr, which is at the wrong offset for struct sockaddr_in6. The resulting IP address string is corrupted/garbage for IPv6 clients. For unexpected address families (e.g. AF_UNSPEC), the same corruption occurs silently.
findings.new_behavior: lookup_hostname() checks ai->ai_family: for AF_INET reads struct sockaddr_in::sin_addr, for AF_INET6 reads struct sockaddr_in6::sin6_addr correctly. For any unexpected address family, it calls die() which terminates the daemon connection with a diagnostic message. inet_ntop() is called with the correct address family.
findings.compatibility_reason: The IP address string stored in hi->ip_address and returned by get_ip_address() changes for IPv6 clients from corrupted to correct. This IP address is used in: (1) daemon repository path interpolation via %%IP format specifier, (2) access hook arguments, (3) daemon logging. The change is a bug fix, but any scripts or hooks that consumed the corrupted IPv6 address will observe a different value. Additionally, unexpected address families now cause daemon connection termination (die()) instead of silent garbage output.
findings.why_not_internal_only: lookup_hostname() is static but its output reaches external consumers via get_ip_address(), which is used in daemon path interpolation (%%IP) and passed as an argument to the access hook script. Both paths are user/script-facing.
findings.uncertainty: Unlikely that any production script depends on the corrupted IPv6 address, but the output string change and new die() path for unusual families are real behavioral changes.
findings.recommended_review: Review if any deployment relies on parsing daemon-IP from logs or hooks when IPv6 clients are connected. The corrupted IPv6 output would have been wrong before, so this fix is almost certainly desired, but the address string content changes.
findings.test_recommendation: Test git daemon with an IPv6 client connection and verify the IP address is correctly formatted. Test with a dual-stack host. Test the die() path by simulating an unexpected address family return.
